name: Liquid ETF Extended
description: Second-stage daily ETF universe for broader campaign discovery after the core ETF campaign loop proved it can run, diversify, and report stop semantics cleanly.
intended_use: factor, sector, bond, commodity, and international ETF comparisons

research_boundary.why_this_next: This expands breadth without jumping to individual stocks, survivorship-sensitive membership history, delisting handling, or event-data infrastructure.
research_boundary.data_policy: Fetch each symbol with quant-lab fetch using adjusted daily yfinance data and keep the generated provenance sidecar beside the ignored cache CSV.

benchmark.role: default buy-and-hold benchmark for broad risk-asset comparisons

groups.rationale: Broad US equity exposures for baseline risk-on comparisons, index leadership, and capitalization/regime differences.
Style and factor ETFs help test whether simple effects are broad-market timing artifacts or behave differently across growth, value, momentum, quality, volatility, and equal-weight exposures.
Sector and industry ETFs support leadership, defensive-sector, crowding, and regime-rotation hypotheses without individual-stock universe maintenance.
Treasury, credit, mortgage, inflation-linked, emerging-market bond, and cashlike ETFs give defensive alternatives and stress different risk-off mechanisms.
Gold, silver, oil, broad commodities, agriculture, real estate, and dollar exposure broaden inflation, crisis, and non-equity diversification hypotheses.
Developed, emerging, regional, and country ETFs support global leadership and diversification tests with simple daily data.

known_caveats: ETF inception dates differ; use data-trust reports to inspect actual overlapping rows before portfolio or cross-symbol conclusions.
Adjusted yfinance OHLCV is convenient but still depends on provider semantics; keep adjusted-price audits separate from strategy conclusions.
Commodity, volatility-sensitive, and futures-holding ETFs can embed roll costs and product-specific mechanics; conclusions are about ETF products, not spot markets.
Some industry and country ETFs are less liquid than SPY or sector SPDRs; use this universe for research breadth, not automatic deployability claims.
This is still mostly institutionally visible ETF territory. It helps campaign discovery, but it is not yet the small-capacity niche layer.
